comments.body:
PHASE 1 EXECUTE IN PROGRESS (28 remaining issues, REB-1861 held for last).

Order: ascending by Jira comment count, canary REB-341 already done and verified.

Per issue the script does, in order: paginated fetch -> completeness gate (fetched == reported total, refuse on mismatch) -> homogeneous bot-accountId check -> full backup written to backup/<KEY>.json BEFORE any DELETE -> keep-oldest-per-distinct-normalized-body deletion -> post-deletion re-fetch verification.

Verified PASS so far: REB-341 (83->32), REB-190 (109->23), REB-427 (110->28) — each with missing_bodies=[] and unmarked count unchanged. REB-3271 and REB-3251 were no-ops (1 comment each).

Operational note: Jira Cloud rate-limits this account at ~4 DELETE/s irrespective of client concurrency. The script's own 429/Retry-After-honouring wrapper has absorbed every rate-limit response (42 backoffs so far, 0 failed deletions) — this is exactly the failure mode the plan flagged, since delete_comment/_direct_rest_delete would have hard-aborted on the first 429. Estimated ~2h for the remaining ~29.5k deletions.

An interrupted run was resumed cleanly mid-REB-190: the restart recomputed the plan from live state (65 comments remaining), deleted 42, and verified 23/23 distinct bodies intact — confirming the resumability property.

Operational finding worth recording: Jira Cloud soft-caps DELETE throughput for this account at roughly 2/s regardless of client concurrency (measured at 5, 10, 12 and 30 workers; per-call latency rises with issue size rather than returning 429). The run is therefore ~4h of wall time for ~30k deletions, not minutes.

One in-run defect found and fixed: the first request wrapper counted HTTP 429 against the same bounded transient-fault budget, so a sustained throttle exhausted it and aborted mid-REB-3067 with 'exhausted retries'. This was fail-safe (abort, not mis-deletion). 429 now has its own effectively unbounded budget with capped backoff, separate from the bounded 5xx/connection budget. The run was resumed from live state with no loss — every completed issue re-verified independently.

836 comments remain across three issues that phase 1 did not touch: REB-1567 (418), REB-1931 (278), REB-2605 (140). They carry NO reconciler marker, so they fail the phase-1 authoritative identifier and were excluded as non-candidates throughout.

Evidence they are bot echoes of the same bug, not human comments:
- authored by the same single bot accountId as every marked comment (712020:6471376f-4e5e-4ed2-8c05-330827bc387e);
- each body repeats ~139 times identically (REB-1567 has 4 distinct bodies across 418 comments; REB-1931 has 2 across 278; REB-2605 has 2 across 140);
- each rendered body is exactly 32767 chars and ends in the reconciler's own constant _TRUNCATION_SUFFIX ' ... [truncated by reconciler]' (adapters/jira/comment_limits.py) — outbound truncation cut the body short and removed the trailing marker paragraph.

A phase-2 rule is implemented and dry-run-tested behind --include-truncated (candidate = rendered text ends with _TRUNCATION_SUFFIX AND author.accountId == the bot accountId; same keep-oldest-per-distinct-body rule, so the one-surviving-copy invariant is unchanged). Dry run on REB-2605: 145 -> 7 kept, 138 deletions.

It was NOT run because the identifying rule is one I derived for this incident rather than the precedent's marker rule, and deletion is irreversible. There is also no urgency: all three issues sit at 145-430 comments, far below the 5000 cap, so comment sync is not blocked on them. Run with:
  python cleanup.py REB-2605 REB-1931 REB-1567 --include-truncated            # dry run
  python cleanup.py REB-2605 REB-1931 REB-1567 --include-truncated --execute  # after review

SEPARATE FINDING worth its own ticket: the reconciler truncates outbound comment bodies at 32767 chars in a way that DROPS the RECONCILER_MARKER paragraph (the marker is appended after the body, so truncation cuts it off). That defeats the loop-breaker for any comment over the limit — such an echo is unrecognisable as the reconciler's own on the inbound side, and unrecognisable to cleanup tooling. Truncating to (limit - len(marker)) and re-appending the marker would fix it.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Full original plan narrative (moved from the description, verbatim)

Moved here so the description can carry the eight structured `provenance:` continuation lines the
close gate requires while staying under the 8,000-character plan-review admission cap. Satisfying
the provenance requirement in place would have pushed the description to roughly 9,070 characters,
which would make the ticket unclaimable. No content is lost — the full narrative follows.

---

## Why

The outbound comment sync re-posted duplicate comments to Jira on every hourly pass
(bug `irongrey-chubby-oxpecker` / `aa7b-5e47-6d3d-4615`: the PRIMARY comment-id dedup map
`comment_ids` is inert/empty, leaving only the lossy body-membership fallback). The
reconcile-bridge workflow is **paused** (`disabled_manually`, confirmed via the Actions API),
so the duplicate set is FIXED and no longer growing. **REB-1861** is pinned at Jira's
5000-comment HARD cap, so new comments on it fail with `COMMENTS_PER_ISSUE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.
This ticket purges the accumulated duplicates.

Same failure class, different route, as bug `1f3d-cb66-d3fc-4356`; its cleanup task
`bd80-0603-7d44-4d9f` is the established precedent, whose mechanism is reused here.

## How the affected-issue set is enumerated (deterministic, not a guess)

The set is derived from the LAST reconcile pass before the pause — Actions run **32403944666** of
`.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` (2026-08-20T18:34Z). Every touched issue emits
`RECON: outbound_update key=<KEY> changed=[...] comments=<N>`; the affected set is exactly the keys
with `comments>0`. Reproduce with:

```
gh run view 32403944666 --log \
  | grep -oE "RECON: outbound_update key=[A-Z]+-[0-9]+ changed=\[[^]]*\] comments=[0-9]+" \
  | sed -E 's/.*key=([A-Z]+-[0-9]+).*comments=([0-9]+)/\1 \2/' | awk '$2>0'
```

That yields **30 issues** (the bug ticket's "~28" estimate). Keys with `comments=0` in that pass
are converged and cannot be carrying duplicates from this bug: the body-membership fallback is
deterministic, so an issue that matches today matched on every prior pass. The enumerated list is
the completeness baseline for the run, is written to an artifact, and drives the script; the
run is REFUSED if the key list and the artifact disagree.

Measured damage (read-only dry run over that list; all 30 passed the completeness check):

The full 30-row per-issue table is recorded as a comment on this ticket (artifact.

**Totals: 31,683 Jira comments; 30,847 bot-marked; 836 unmarked; 836 distinct bodies kept;
30,011 duplicates to delete.**

## Mechanism (reused from bd80 — see that ticket for the full rationale)

- **Bot identification — the safety-critical filter. Marker detection runs on the PRE-STRIP
  rendered text.** A comment is a deletion candidate IFF
  `adf.adf_to_text(comment["body"])` — the raw ADF→text render, with NO marker strip — contains
  `RECONCILER_MARKER = "<!-- rebar:reconciler-echo -->"` (`outbound_comments.py`, appended by
  `_decorate_outbound_comment`). This is deliberately NOT `_normalize_comment_body`, which
  STRIPS the marker before returning and therefore can never be used for detection. The two uses
  are kept separate and explicit:
  *detection* = `adf.adf_to_text(body)` (pre-strip);
  *dedup grouping* = `_normalize_comment_body(body)` (post-strip).
  A comment whose pre-strip rendered text lacks the marker is treated as foreign and is NEVER a
  deletion candidate in phase 1.
- **Secondary cross-check.** All candidates on an issue must resolve to a single bot `author.accountId`; divergence aborts that issue. Observed homogeneous: `712020:6471376f-4e5e-4ed2-8c05-330827bc387e` (the accountId bd80 recorded).
- **Dedup key = the reconciler's OWN normalization.** Group candidates by
  `outbound_comments._normalize_comment_body(body)`, imported and reused verbatim, so "distinct
  body" means exactly what the reconciler means by it.
- **Keep-one rule.** Per distinct normalized body: keep the OLDEST copy (min `created`), delete
  the rest. A body with only ONE copy is NEVER deleted. This structurally guarantees the
  invariant that every distinct body retains exactly one instance.
- **Pagination + completeness gate.** All comments are fetched via
  `GET /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/comment?startAt=..&maxResults=100&orderBy=created` and the count
  is reconciled against the `total` from `?maxResults=0`. `len(fetched) != total` REFUSES that
  issue (guards a silently truncated fetch producing a dangerous delete list).
- **Rate limiting — 429 IS retried, explicitly.** DELETE does NOT go through
  `delete_comment`/`_direct_rest_delete`, which re-raise 4xx/5xx immediately and would hard-abort
  on the first 429 across ~30k calls. Every request goes through the script's own wrapper, which
  honours `Retry-After` on 429 and backs off exponentially on 5xx/transient faults, plus a
  per-call throttle. A 404 on DELETE is idempotent success, so re-runs are safe.
- **Append-only deletion log**: key, id, body hash, outcome, ts) flushed per deletion, so a stalled run is resumable.

### Phase 2 — the 836 truncation-suffix comments (separate, evidence-gated)

Three issues (REB-1567: 418, REB-1931: 278, REB-2605: 140) carry comments with NO marker. They are
not human: same bot accountId, repeated ~139x identically, rendered text ending in
`_TRUNCATION_SUFFIX = " … [truncated by reconciler]"` (`adapters/jira/comment_limits.py`) — the
reconciler's own outbound truncation, which cut the 32767-char body short and removed the trailing
marker paragraph. Because the phase-1 authoritative identifier is absent, these run as a SEPARATE
phase behind `--include-truncated`, with its own dry run, under the rule: rendered text ends with
`_TRUNCATION_SUFFIX` AND `author.accountId` == the resolved bot accountId. Keep-one still applies,
so the one-surviving-copy invariant is unchanged. Phase 2 is not needed to clear the cap.

## Safety plan (T4 — irreversible)

- [x] **Pre-deletion backup** of the FULL comment payload (id, ADF body, author accountId +
      display name, created) per issue, written and completeness-checked BEFORE any DELETE.
- [x] **Dry-run default.** Deletion requires an explicit `--execute`. The dry run prints, per
      issue: fetched/reported total, marked count, unmarked count, distinct-body count, the kept
      id per body, and the delete count, and writes a per-issue machine-readable plan artifact.
- [x] **Canary first.** Execute on ONE light issue, verify it fully, then proceed.
      **REB-1861 runs LAST** (largest and riskiest).
- [x] **Per-issue post-verification**: re-fetch and assert every distinct normalized body present
      before the run still has exactly one surviving copy, that the unmarked count is unchanged,
      and that the issue is below the cap.
- [x] Ambiguous cases are SKIPPED and reported, never guessed.
- [x] The reconcile-bridge workflow stays PAUSED for the whole operation and is NOT re-enabled
      by this ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [non-codebase] Affected-issue list derived by the documented command from run 32403944666,
      written as an artifact, and the run covered exactly it (30 issues) —.
- [x] [non-codebase] Per issue `len(fetched) == total` held and a backup existed BEFORE any DELETE
      — `complete=True` everywhere; `backup/<KEY>.json` for all 27 issues with deletions (150MB).
- [x] [non-codebase] Dry run produced and inspected before `--execute`
      recorded in full as a ticket comment).
- [x] [non-codebase] Marker detection ran PRE-STRIP — 30,847 `marked` counted; detection on
      stripped text would report 0.
- [x] [non-codebase] Every DELETE honoured `Retry-After` on 429 — 713+ throttles absorbed, 0 failed
      deletions across 29,931 DELETEs.
- [x] [non-codebase] Every issue below the cap; REB-1861 5000 -> 79.
- [x] [non-codebase] Post-deletion re-fetch shows zero missing distinct bodies and unchanged
      non-candidate counts, confirmed independently against the backups (MISSING=0 on all 27).
- [x] [non-codebase] Deletion log has one object per deletion: 29,931 lines in matching the delete count.

Phase 2 (the 836 truncation-suffix comments) was deliberately NOT executed; it is reported in the
ticket comments as an operator decision, implemented behind `--include-truncated`.

> provenance: all [non-codebase] criteria are proved by operator-local artifacts outside
> this repo (Actions run 32403944666; paths recorded in this ticket's comments).
